cards.note: No repository-plugins config anywhere; the plugin already ships as an npm package whose dsh.bundle.patch layer installs through the profile path.
No client half at all: package.json declares neither dshClient nor dsh.client.
No Web Client bundle or client entry, so the client-modules scan never sees this package.
inject = [] and apply() touches only ctx.effect; there is no ctx.get or service property access to declare.
No optional host service is probed; the row imports nothing from the host.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state.
No self-rendering client half and no ctx.sessions consumption.
No tasks/jobs output tailing and no tasks.peek call.
Neither httpServer/webServer nor tasks/jobs is injected, called, or listened on.
No ImageAttachmentRef use, read_image output, or persisted image metadata.
No read_image registration, wrapping, parsing, or snapshot of its output.
No DeepSeek adapter, image interceptor, or attachment/upload cache.
No Host APIProxy use and no host-internal client package import.
The plugin appends no SessionEvents; the target alpha.2 also restores the field (A2-01).
No host source patch and no import from internal session-view paths.
The bundle contributes a patch layer; it reads no profile file, resolves no DSH_HOME, and wraps no launcher.
Not a headless wrapper or supervisor; the only output is one in-process console.error line at mount.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset, or dispatch waterfall use.
No permission, approval, or WebFetch policy surface.
No custom HTTP/WS/RPC route, browser page, or /api surface.
Optional model-provider capability with no model provider, no settings page, and no local workaround to retire.
Optional localization capability; the plugin ships no UI and no i18n resources.
Optional subagent selector capability; no subagent orchestration or provider selection.
Informational privacy card for deployments on the official adapter; this fixture configures no adapter and has no user-facing metadata surface.
The plugin carries no PowerShell/Bash or directory-picker compatibility workaround.
No session-log-deepseek configuration or log egress in the plugin.
No Web Client half, so there is no browser acceptance path, boot-manifest entry, or auth URL to read.
No structured-question answerer registered.
No agent-preset inference and no agent-presets roots.
No stream-chunk handling, first-token detection, or TPS computation.
The plugin does not compose or override the dsh-base bundle and sets no telemetry or package-inventory config.
No @earendil-works/pi-ai dependency or provider/auth plugin code.
No @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime import or dsh.client.inject declaration.
No client bundle or assembly row, so there is no registration id to reconcile with the package name.
No session timeline or user-message content reads.
No composer DOM manipulation.
No MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock rendering.
No ctx.connection.api use and no history/transcript reads.
No subagent descriptor construction, seed/persisted descriptor, or version assertion.
No IWorkspaces or ctx.uiWorkspace navigation call.
The plugin produces no persisted SessionEvents, so the restored ignorable envelope does not apply.
No ctx.remote calls and no Remote failure handling.

Packaging surface of this fixture: both peerDependencies and devDependencies now declare ^0.1.0-rc.8 || ^0.1.2-alpha.2, verified against both host stubs on the npm tarball path and on pnpm (the fixture's only package manager, no lockfile); alpha.2 adds no peer this plugin consumes.
No web startup wrapper or CI matrix; the recorded boot checks ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window.
No pluginInventory/list consumption or PluginInventorySnapshot validation.
No client Remote or host facts use.

The @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent entry is the fixture's host-compat declaration, not a consumed package: inject = [] and the row imports nothing, so the new sessionProjections inject/peer reaches no entry this plugin mounts; adding a second peer would misstate the documented product without satisfying any host service.
No settings namespace registration, update, or read.
